title: AIVV Finding Envelope
description: Machine-parseable envelope for a single IV&V finding. Emitted as JSONL by aivv:reviewer AFTER the prose review. Consumed by /aivv-fix Step 1 COLLECT, wont-fix registry fingerprinting, and multi-reviewer consensus dedup. Envelope only — the full investigator schema (skills/aivv-fix/references/json-schema.md) extends this with root-cause analysis, codebase scan, fix proposal, and prevention mechanism fields. Citation evidence per dev.18 reviewer-grounding methodology may be carried in two forms: the typed `grounded_by` array (preferred, dev.31+) or as legacy free-form `grounded_by:{<source_type>:<source_ref>}` substrings inside `summary` (accepted during the migration window). Readers MUST handle both forms.

id.description: Finding ID assigned by the reviewer or orchestrator. Format: F001, F002, ..., F999+.

severity.description: Severity classification. CRITICAL: immediate blocker or safety issue. MAJOR: real issue requiring fix. MINOR: low-impact, may defer. POLISH (dev.39+): improvement opportunity / value-add suggestion (NOT a defect tier — orthogonal to CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR). Reviewer must establish verified present need, a specific Improvement, and positive net Value per the Improvement-articulation pass in .aivv/methodology.md; if any is missing, drop the finding rather than emit POLISH.

confidence.description: Reviewer confidence in the finding. HIGH: directly observed in code/evidence. MEDIUM: strong inference. LOW: speculative — should pair with additional context.

likelihood.description: Probability the harmful condition is reached and triggered at the current real-world inputs — reasoned through reachability × exposure × trigger-conditionality (will-it-manifest). Distinct from `confidence`, which is existence-certainty (is-it-real): a finding can be HIGH-confidence-real yet UNLIKELY to trigger, or vice-versa. CERTAIN: triggers on every / the common path. PROBABLE: triggers under ordinary real-world conditions. POSSIBLE: needs a specific but reachable condition. UNLIKELY: rare path, narrow input, or seldom-hit branch. Optional; consumed by the impact×likelihood severity model (`severity_model: impact_likelihood`) where it pairs with `impact_tier` in the 4×4 cell-map. Absent under the default `legacy_4pass`. See the project's severity-model decision records.

impact_tier.description: Magnitude of harm if the finding is real AND triggered — reasonable worst-case, anchored to observable harm categories (data loss/corruption, auth/authz bypass, financial loss, core-task failure, legal/compliance exposure, cosmetic) and NEVER to reviewer prose tone. CATASTROPHIC: data loss/corruption, auth/authz bypass, or equivalent irreversible/financial harm. SEVERE: core-task failure or significant legal/compliance exposure. MODERATE: degraded-but-recoverable experience. NEGLIGIBLE: cosmetic / no functional harm. Optional; pairs with `likelihood` in the impact×likelihood severity model's 4×4 cell-map (`severity_model: impact_likelihood`). Absent under the default `legacy_4pass`. See the project's severity-model decision records.

category.description: Finding category aligned with /aivv-fix Step 2 triage classification. `improvement` (dev.146+): a behaviour-preserving betterment (clarity, complexity reduction, redundancy removal, ergonomics) rather than a defect — orthogonal to defect severity. Renders as POLISH and may be prioritized by optional `value`/`effort` metadata (Quick Wins); a behaviour-preserving betterment is never a defect tier. Routes to Step 5 Branch F (scoped simplification, behaviour-preserving).

summary.description: One-line human-readable summary of the finding. Keep under ~200 characters for readable diff output.

value.description: Optional improvement-track prominence metadata. Use only for `category: improvement` / POLISH findings after verified present need and positive net value are established: high = clearly valuable simplification, maintainability, or clarity now; medium = useful but not urgent; low = marginal. Hypothetical future-proofing alone is insufficient. Used only for sorting/prominence within POLISH, never as a defect severity tier.

effort.description: Optional improvement-track cost metadata. Use only for `category: improvement` / POLISH findings: trivial = small localized edit; moderate = bounded multi-step change; invasive = broad or structural change. Used with `value` for Quick-Win prominence; invasive improvements remain advisory unless separately authorized.

quality_profile.description: When present, this finding uses the strict modern new-write profile. Legacy findings may omit this field and remain readable.

scope_ref.description: Stable non-file scope for process/session/artifact findings. Use instead of inventing fake file paths.

evidence.description: Concrete evidence that makes the finding reproducible.

proportional_remediation.description: The minimum-sufficient-remediation decision for this recommended change. New modern findings must state the current problem, smallest adequate correction, added/removed moving pieces, and why no change or a smaller local correction is insufficient.

file.description: File path (repo-relative) where the finding is located. Omit or null for findings without a code location (e.g., process, documentation-gap on the whole project).

line.description: 1-indexed line number within `file`. Omit or null if not applicable.

reviewer.description: Reviewer label. 'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma', ... for N-way consensus runs; 'solo' for N=1. Enables cross-reviewer dedup and consensus synthesis.

lens.description: Review lens. Shipped lenses (one entry per lens file under .aivv/lenses/): general (broad goal-fit, evidence, design, and risk review), code (default for legacy findings), sec (security; dev.22+), visual (UI/a11y/component correctness; dev.22+), ux (heuristic walkthrough + microcopy + interaction states; dev.43+), polish (improvement-articulation / value-add; dev.43+), compliance (WCAG AAA + ARIA APG full + legal-risk subset; dev.105), i18n (translation discipline + CLDR + Intl.* + RTL; dev.105), user-journey (UJ-* rules; dev.121). Forward-look planned lenses retained for compatibility with calibration corpora that may pre-emit them: perf (performance review; planned Tier 2/3), a11y (pure-a11y split distinct from visual lens's UI-a11y; planned Tier 2/3). Findings without this field continue to default to 'code'.

rule_id.description: Optional stable rule identifier from .aivv/standards/<file>.md. Pattern enforces the documented prefix space (per .aivv/standards/README.md rule-ID prefix table): A11Y-* (accessibility.md), UX-* (ui-ux.md), MC-* (microcopy.md), VVT-* (visual-verification-triggers.md), HEU-* (ux-heuristics.md, shipped dev.46), IS-* (interaction-states.md, shipped dev.46), VD-* (visual-design.md, shipped dev.54), DP-*/COMP-*/I18N-*/RTV-* (planned standards files), SEC-* (security rule-ID space), UJ-* (user-journey.md, shipped dev.121), AS-* (architecture.md cross-file/structure catalog, shipped dev.147), CQ-* (code-quality.md code-simplification catalog, shipped dev.109 — prefix added to this pattern at dev.148, correcting a dev.109 omission). Forward-look prefixes (DP/COMP/I18N/RTV/SEC) are accepted today so reviewers can cite them once their backing standards files ship; lens files instruct reviewers to use grounded_by[*].source_type='unverifiable' for pre-shipped prefixes (see .aivv/lenses/ux.md Forward-reference rule). Read by the orchestrator for L1-source forced-override (per skills/aivv-fix/references/polish-and-l1-source-policy.md L1-source detection logic) and by per-rule FP/TP calibration aggregators (per .aivv/calibration/README.md). Pre-dev.41 findings emitted without rule_id remain valid; the field is optional everywhere.

devils_advocate.description: True if the finding was surfaced by the Devil's Advocate Challenge (pre-mortem / assumption inventory / inversion test / simpler-path test). Two+ reviewers independently marking true is the highest-confidence adversarial signal.

grounded_by.description: Structured citation evidence backing the finding (graduated to typed field in dev.31; previously a free-form substring in `summary` per dev.18 reviewer-grounding methodology). PREFERRED form for dev.31+ emissions. The legacy `grounded_by:{<source_type>:<source_ref>}` substring form inside `summary` remains accepted during the migration window — readers MUST handle both forms. Absence is valid: not every finding rests on a groundable claim.

source_type.description: Citation source category. `websearch` / `webfetch` for URLs surfaced via WebSearch / WebFetch. `context7` for library identifiers from Context7 MCP (form: `<library-id>@<version>`). `runtime` for orchestrator-captured runtime artifacts such as axe-core output, computed-style contrast records, screenshots, or screenshot diffs. `internal-repo` for repo-relative paths used as evidence (verify by Grep, not external source). `unverified` when no external grounding was applied. `unverifiable` when the claim was attempted-but-failed to ground (no authoritative source located). The `unverifiable` value is preserved for parity with skills/methodology/SKILL.md emission contract.

source_ref.description: URL, library identifier (`<id>@<version>` for context7), or repo-relative path (for internal-repo). For `unverified` / `unverifiable`, a one-line label describing what was not grounded.

excerpt.description: Optional short excerpt or quote from the source supporting the claim. Helps consumers verify the citation without re-fetching.
